package_info.package_versions: Wallpapers Blur HD, Booster & Cleaner Pro (all versions with LeakerLocker)
package_info.why_malicious: The applications contain embedded ransomware code that abuses granted permissions to harvest personal data (including contacts, photos, messages, and other sensitive information) from the victim's device. The stolen data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled servers, and the user is extorted via a ransom note threatening to publicly leak the data unless a payment is made. This behavior constitutes both privacy violation and extortion.

execution_context.file_location: Main application code (Wallpapers Blur HD / Booster & Cleaner Pro)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application start, the code collects personal data from the device (contacts, photos, messages), exfiltrates this data to a remote attacker-controlled server via network communication, and displays a ransom note threatening to leak the data unless payment is made.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code harvests sensitive user data (contacts, photos, messages) without user consent, transmits it to an external server controlled by the attacker, and then displays a ransom note demanding payment under threat of public exposure. This sequence of actions is characteristic of mobile ransomware and data-leak extortion malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications do not collect and exfiltrate sensitive user data without explicit user consent, nor do they threaten users with data leaks or demand ransom payments. Standard apps must clearly disclose data collection and provide privacy controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or cloud sync applications may collect and upload user data, but only with explicit user consent, transparent privacy policies, and secure, trusted endpoints. They never threaten users or demand ransom.
key_indicators: Automated collection of contacts, photos, and SMS messages at app start
Transmission of harvested data to external, attacker-controlled servers
Display of a ransom note threatening to leak user data unless payment is made
Use of broad permissions (contacts, storage, SMS, camera, internet) not justified by app functionality

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious app from Google Play and grants requested permissions (contacts, storage, SMS, camera, internet).
attack_chain.leads_to: App is able to access sensitive personal data on the device.

attack_chain.action: On application start, the app collects personal data (contacts, photos, messages, etc.) from the device using the granted permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is harvested and prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The app sends the harvested personal data to an attacker-controlled remote server over the internet.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains possession of the victim's sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: The app displays a ransom note to the user, threatening to leak the stolen data unless a ransom payment is made.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is extorted and pressured to pay the ransom to prevent data exposure.

behavioral_signatures: Mobile application collects and exfiltrates personal data (contacts, photos, messages) immediately after installation or on first launch, without user interaction or consent.
Application displays a ransom note threatening to leak user data unless a payment is made.
Network communication to external, attacker-controlled servers following data collection.
file_indicators: Android apps named 'Wallpapers Blur HD' or 'Booster & Cleaner Pro' requesting excessive permissions (contacts, storage, SMS, camera, internet).
Presence of code accessing contacts, photos, SMS, and transmitting data over the network within the main application logic.
network_indicators: Outbound connections from the app to suspicious or known attacker infrastructure immediately after app start or installation.
Data exfiltration to remote servers not associated with legitimate cloud or backup services.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request broad permissions (contacts, storage, SMS, camera, internet) and subsequently access and transmit personal data to external servers, especially if followed by the display of a ransom note or extortion message. Flag apps that display ransom demands or threaten to leak user data. Use network monitoring to detect exfiltration of sensitive data to untrusted or suspicious domains, and correlate with app installation events.
